  COVID-19 PUBLIC SERVICE ANNOUNCEMENT REGARDING MEETINGS OF
  THE INGLEWOOD CITY COUNCIL AND OTHER CITY LEGISLATIVE BODIES

Until further notice, meetings of the Inglewood City Council and other City legislative bodies will be conducted
pursuant to California Government Code section 54953(e), which allows the City to use teleconferencing for
members of the public to access a meeting and to address the legislative body via a call-in option.

CALL-IN OPTION

1. Members of the public who wish to attend a public meeting and address the City Council or other
legislative body during a public meeting must use the call-in option noted below:

  l  Members of the public may listen and make oral public comments telephonically by dialing:
  l Dial-in for Closed Session: 1-669-900-6833 Meeting ID: 825 5030 7638 Passcode: 024788
  l Dial-in for Open Session: 1-888-251-2949 or 215-861-0694, using the specific
  access codes detailed below for the respective City Council Dates:

  l  October 18, 2022 – Access Code: 4345213# wait 3 seconds and press # again
  l  October 25, 2022 – Access Code: 1207201# wait 3 seconds and press # again

In the event of a disruption which prevents the City from broadcasting the meeting to the public using the call-in
option, or in the event of a disruption within the City’s control which prevents the public from offering public
comments using the call-in option, the City Council and other legislative body shall take no further action on items
appearing on the meeting agenda until public access to the meeting via the call-in option is restored.
 In the event of a disruption which prevents the City from broadcasting the meeting to the public using the call-in
option, or in the event of a disruption within the City’s control which prevents the public from offering public
comments using the call-in option, the City Council and other legislative body shall take no further action on items
appearing on the meeting agenda until public access to the meeting via the call-in option is restored.

ALTERNATIVE METHODS

The City also provides alternative methods for members of the public to submit comments and/or to observe a public
meeting. The following alternative methods are provided to the public as a matter of convenience only and the
disruption in service to any alternative method does not preclude the City Council or other legislative body from
taking further action on an agenda item. In the event of a disruption to any alternative method below members of the
public should use the call-in option above.

2. Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may choose to submit comments
electronically for consideration by the City Council or other City Legislative Body by sending them to the City
Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure
distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit comments prior
to 8:00 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda number or subject matter.
Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received after 8:00 a.m. and prior to the
close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public record of the meeting. Contact the Office of the City
Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

3. Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:

  l  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider for
  details.
  l  Live online through Facebook Live, with audio and limited video, at
  https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/

4. Public attendance at Gladys Waddingham Lecture Hall (located adjacent to the Main Library) to view
meeting and make public comments via audio/video.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate alternative
formats to persons with a disability, as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (42
U.S.C. Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and regulations adopted in implementation thereof. Any person who
requires a disability-related modification or accommodation, or translation services in order to observe and/or offer
public comment may request such reasonable modification, accommodation, or service by contacting the Office of
the City Clerk by telephone at 310-412-5280, FAX at 310-412-5533, One Manchester Boulevard, First Floor,
Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA 90301 or via email to athompson@cityofinglewood.org and
aallen@cityofinglewood.org no later than 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting.

Inglewood, California
  October 18, 2022

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
October 18, 2022, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Butts called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:00 p.m.
The Acting City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:
  Present:  Mayor Butts, Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales,
  and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Angela Allen  Acting City Clerk
  Artie Fields  City Manager
  Ken Campos  City Attorney

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEMS. Mayor Butts
inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council on the
Closed Session Item Nos. CS-1 and CS-2.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:01 p.m. for Closed Session Item
Nos. CS-1 and CS-2

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Parking
Authority, and Joint Powers Authority at the hour of 2:02 p.m.
The City Clerk/ Successor Agency Secretary/ Housing Authority Secretary/ Parking
Authority Secretary/ Joint Powers Authority Secretary announced the presence of a
quorum as follows:

  Parking Authority Chairman/ Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts,
  Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority
  Members/ Parking Authority Members/ Joint Powers Authority
  Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent: None.

officials and personnel present were as follows:

  Artie Fields  City Manager/ Executive Director*

  Caller (Name Unknown) spoke about the upcoming elections and the Mayor reading the
  Rules of Decorum. She addressed how the Mayor speaks to the residents, and the lack of
  available resources. She stated that she remained without hot water for 15 months during
  COVID, and believed Titles 2, 3, 6, and 9 were being violated. Finally, she addressed the
  Police Oversight meetings.

  Caller (Name Unknown) spoke on October 20, 2022, not only being the Great Shake Out
  but also the birthday of Mr. Willie Agee. The caller paid homage to Mr. Agee, with his
  favorite saying of “I love living in the beautiful City of Inglewood.”

  Josephine Scott spoke about Ordinance No. 22-15, which was adopted on July 19, 2022.
  She complained about the rate of the Transient Occupancy Tax being 15.5% and
  requested that it be aligned with surrounding counties. She stated 90 to 120 days was not
  enough time because COVID made it challenging for people financially. Finally, she stated
  it was unfair to treat owners who hosts Airbnb like businesses.

  Patty Rivas spoke about Ordinance No. 22-15, which was adopted on July 19, 2022. She
  stated the Transient Occupancy Tax (TOT) rates were high. The caller also stated that she
  shouldn't be allowed to pay the taxes from the beginning of January until the present
  because, she didn’t know they were due. Additionally, she added that surrounding cities’
  taxes are lower, and asked for the same treatment as other cities. Finally, she asked the
  Council to reconsider the requirement for her to pay the TOT.
